Hi Ben,

We're finalizing our vendor review for the SecureLife integration and need a couple of items from Redwood to close our privacy/compliance gating. Because this integration will pass protected health information (PHI) in production, our legal team needs: 

- A current vendor/subprocessor roster (including vendor name, role, processing location(s), and whether they onward-transfer outside the US).
- Confirmation if any subprocessors perform backups or logging that store PHI outside the US (EU, APAC). - Copies: SOC 2 summary or report, and a template BAA you are willing to sign.
- If there are any onward-transfer consents you provide to customers (explicit permissions or checkbox consent) please share the exact text/DocuSign link.

Can you get us the roster and quick answers by EOD Thursday (16 Sep)? If Redwood requires a formal request or PO to provide detailed vendor contact information, let me know.

Hi all — attaching the current vendor roster (vendor-roster-2026.csv), our SOC 2 executive summary (SOC2-summary-2026.pdf), and the standard BAA template (BAA_Template_Redwood.docx). See notes below: 

1) Vendor roster: the CSV includes name, primary processing role, primary processing region, and whether the vendor may onward-transfer. For each vendor we mark "onward_transfer_allowed" = yes/no and a short explanation.

2) LogStream (observability): LogStream receives aggregated logs. By default we strip user-provided document bodies and PII from logs; however, customers can enable full-request logging for debugging which may capture PHI. LogStream operates EU and US regions. For HIPAA customers we: 
   - Recommend region-locking (EU/US) so logs persist only in the chosen region.
   - Provide a consent form (DocuSign) to explicitly authorize LogStream to process logs that may contain PHI in the EU.

3) Onward-transfer permissions: Redwood does not unilaterally permit downstream transfers of PHI beyond subprocessors in our roster without a customer-level consent where required by law. Where a subprocessor itself uses downstream processors (e.g., a backup vendor used by a storage vendor), we capture that subprocessor chain and disclose it in the roster.

4) BAAs: we will sign a BAA. The attached template is our standard form; we are open to narrow redlines on sections related to liability caps and data return/destruction.

Next steps suggested: 
- Ben: propose we send SecureLife a one-click DocuSign for the LogStream onward-transfer consent and the BAA template for signature.
- Laura: please confirm any residual risk and whether we need a short mitigation we can apply until we receive signed consents.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
